Identifier of a physical location (room). With the advent of bar coding, it is essential that this field uniquely and unambiguously specify a particular location. Entries may consist of one, two, or three pieces. Hyphens (if present) are treated as delimiters between pieces. First piece (always present) is room designation, second piece (optional) is building designation, and third piece (optional) is division designation (may be used for outpatient clinics, regional offices, etc. as well as for formal divisions).  It is anticipated that most sites will use two piece entries. True single-building facilities may use one-piece entries. Multi-division facilities and sites supporting remote offices where duplicate building numbers may be a problem should use three-piece entries.  Entry of a two-piece ROOM NUMBER will automatically populate the BUILDING field. Entry of a three-piece ROOM NUMBER will automatically populate the BUILDING and DIVISION fields.  Hyphens must not be used as anything other than delimiters between ROOM, BUILDING, and DIVISION.

A classification agreed on by the VA and its oversight agencies for Y2K compliance reporting.  PC =>  A general purpose personal computer or workstation used for office applications. Not an integral part of a medical device or of a facility management system.  MED => Medical devices are pieces of equipment (or equipment systems) that are dedicated to the diagnosis and/or treatment of patients. Includes anything that requires Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approval as a medical device before it can be commercially marketed to health care providers in the United States.  FS =>  Facility systems (or facility equipment) are devices (or equipment systems) used to manage the environment of care within health care facilities. Includes building service equipment of all types, such as: o Emergency communications management systems o Security systems o Alarm systems o Fire detection and control systems o Environmental control systems o Water management o Electrical energy management and control systems o Building transport systems (people and/or material)  TEL => Telecommunications equipment, broadly defined. This classification includes PBX systems, voice mail, radio frequency communication systems, faxes, routers, switches, bridges, servers, modems, satellite communication systems, video conferencing, and wireless LAN.

Make a separate entry for each category (MONTHLY, QUARTERLY, etc.) of PMI that is to be scheduled for this device. The PM module looks at this field in conjunction with the STARTING MONTH when PM lists are generated. Let's consider a fairly complex example: a device with SEMI-ANNUAL, QUARTERLY, and MONTHLY PMI's and a STARTING MONTH of MAR. Assuming no entry for SKIP MONTHS, the following PMI's will be scheduled: SEMI-ANNUAL in MAR and SEP; QUARTERLY in JUN and DEC; MONTHLY in APR, MAY, JUL, AUG, OCT, NOV, JAN and FEB.

Approximate amount of time required for this PMI(standard hours), to the nearest tenth of an hour. This value will be recorded in the EQUIPMENT HISTORY field when a PM is closed out unless the user chooses to explicitly enter another (more precise) value.

Each scheduled PMI may be composed of some combination of one or more of the following discrete levels of activity: Level 1 - Visual inspection only; Level 2 - Check and adjust operator controls; Level 3 - Electrical safety analysis; Level 4 - Minor parts replacement; Level 5 - Major parts replacement; Level 6 - Complete overhaul. LEVEL is an optional field and is intended to accommodate the needs of certain facilities with highly developed PM programs. Entries for LEVEL (if any) will be printed on the PM worklist as a reminder to the responsible technician. If more than one number applies, separate numbers a comma.

The closer the values are to the upper limit the more critical the PMI's become. A value of 1 would indicate that PMI's are desireable but far from essential (least critical).  When PM worklists are generated, the system will ask if all devices should be included or just those whose CRITICALITY is within a certain user selectable range (say, 7 to 10). This is intended as a means of adjusting workload to match available resources.  Use of this feature is left entirely to the discretion of each site. A range of months (inclusive) during which PMI's are to be suspended. For example, an entry of 'NOV-MAR' for an air-conditioner would suppress the scheduling of any PMI's in NOV, DEC, JAN, FEB, and MAR. Some care needs to be taken when using this field. If you want an ANNUAL inspecton, for instance, be sure that the STARTING MONTH is not within the range specified by the SKIP MONTHS; otherwise the ANNUAL PMI will never be scheduled. Entries must take the form 'MMM-NNN', where MMM is a three character abbreviation of the first month for which PMiI's are to be suspended and NNN is a three character abbreviation for the last month for which PMI's are to be suspended. Valid abbreviations are: JAN, FEB, MAR, APR, MAY, JUN, JUL, AUG, SEP, OCT, NOV, and DEC.

STARTING MONTH is used by the PM module as a criterion for determining when a PM is due. Let's consider a fairly complex example: an item subject to MONTHLY, QUARTERLY, and ANNUAL PM inspections. If STARTING MONTH were set to FEB; an ANNUAL inspection would be scheduled in FEB; QUARTERLY inspections in MAY, AUG, and NOV; and MONTHLY inspections in MAR, APR, JUN, JUL, SEP, OCT, DEC, and JAN. EQUIPMENT_INV_6914.PURCHASE_ORDER_: VA Purchase Order number. May be assigned by the facility or perhaps by a centralized purchasing unit of the Office of Acquisitions and Material Management.
EQUIPMENT_INV_6914.REMAIN_CAPITALIZED_SE: This field has been temporarily added to the EQUIPMENT INV file by patch EN*7*71 for management of the one-time capitalization threshold task. This task will expense equipment that is currently capitalized and reported to Fixed Assets/FMS, but does not meet the new capitalization threshold of $100,000. After the one-time task has run on July 24, 2002, this field will be obsolete and it will be deleted by a subsequent patch.  This field can be updated by the Adjust List of Equipment to be Expensed by Task option.  If this field is populated then the associated equipment item will not be expensed even though it meets the other criteria to be expensed.
EQUIPMENT_INV_6914.REPLACEMENT_DATE: Date on which this equipment is scheduled for replacement. Month and year are sufficient. When equipment is entered, this field should be the ACQUISITION DATE plus the LIFE EXPECTANCY. As scheduled REPLACEMENT DATE is approached, however, it may be necessary to revise it. Such revisions do not always alter the official LIFE EXPECTANCY.
EQUIPMENT_INV_6914.REPLACEMENT_UPDATE_CO: Codes: 4=NOT TO BE REPLACED, 5=TO BE REPLACED UNDER ACTIVATION PROJECT, 6=ON ORDER
EQUIPMENT_INV_6914.REPLACING_ENTRY_NUMBE: If this item was acquired as REPLACEMENT EQUIPMENT, then the old ENTRY NUMBER of the item which it replaced should appear in this field.
EQUIPMENT_INV_6914.SERIAL_: Serial number. Assigned by manufacturer. Should be unique within model and manufacturer. Use numbers, upper case letters, punctuation, and spaces as needed.
EQUIPMENT_INV_6914.SERIAL_C: This field contains a compressed value of the SERIAL # field. The computer automatically populates this field by stripping the SERIAL # of punctuation and spaces and changing any lowercase characters to uppercase.
EQUIPMENT_INV_6914.SERVICE_CONTRACT: YES indicates that device in question is under a service contract with an entity outside the medical center. A more comprehensive module for service contracts is being developed jointly by AEMS/MERS and IFCAP and will appear in a future release.
EQUIPMENT_INV_6914.SERVICE_CONTRACT_COST: Annual cost of service contract on this item. If contract involves one fixed amount for a number of like devices, you should prorate the cost among the covered items.
EQUIPMENT_INV_6914.SERVICE_POINTER: The functional entity (generally a service) within the facility that uses the device.
EQUIPMENT_INV_6914.SOURCE_OF_Y2K_CATEGOR: The source of the Y2K categorization for this item. This required field will default to "Local assessment" and will not appear on any packaged reports. You may access the information via VA FileMan if you need it.  "Local assessment" generally means that specific information from the VA web site and/or the device manufacturer is unavailable (and perhaps unnecessary). In these cases, Y2K categorization is made on the basis of the professional opinion of facility management staff.  Sites are cautioned against attempting to perform actual Y2K compliance tests on equipment that may have Y2K problems because advanced date simulation in systems with embedded microprocessors may be very difficult to achieve.
Codes: VA=VA WEB SITE, MAN=MANUFACTURER WEB SITE OR LETTER, LOC=LOCAL ASSESSMENT
EQUIPMENT_INV_6914.STANDARD_GENERAL_LEDG: In accordance with the VA administrative accounting system. Only a limited number of Standard General Ledger Accounts are appropriate for use with non-expendable equipment.
EQUIPMENT_INV_6914.STATION_NUMBER: Station number of the facility that owns this equipment. If this equipment is owned by a national cemetery that is serviced by a VAMC, then the station number of the cemetery should appear in this field.
EQUIPMENT_INV_6914.SUBACCOUNT: NOTE: This field is not used and it will be deleted by a future version.
EQUIPMENT_INV_6914.TOTAL_ASSET_VALUE: Cost of this equipment at the time of purchase. This field is likely to become the basis for estimating depreciated value and replacement cost.
EQUIPMENT_INV_6914.TURNIN_DATE: Date on which item is turned over to A&MM for disposition.  At this point it should be removed from the using service CMR.
EQUIPMENT_INV_6914.TYPE_OF_ENTRY: Discriminates between entries for which a CMR Official is legally responsible and those that are accounted for in other ways.
Codes: NX=NON-EXPENDABLE EQPT, BSE=BUILDING SERVICE EQPT, EXP=EXPENDABLE EQPT
EQUIPMENT_INV_6914.USE_STATUS: Tells the user whether or not the equipment is currently in active use.
Codes: 1=IN USE, 2=OUT OF SERVICE, 3=LOANED OUT, 4=TURNED IN, 5=LOST OR STOLEN
EQUIPMENT_INV_6914.VA_PM_NUMBER: Property management number. Assigned by Supply Service upon receipt of new equipment. Should be unique within the facility. First four digits correspond to the Federal Supply Classification number.
EQUIPMENT_INV_6914.VENDOR_POINTER: Vendor from whom unit was actually purchased.
EQUIPMENT_INV_6914.WARRANTY_EXP__DATE: Date on which repairs to this item become the sole responsibility of the government. Generally stipulated in the contract or sales agreement.
EQUIPMENT_INV_6914.Y2K_ACTION: This field should be populated only for devices that are Y2K NON-COMPLIANT. It indicates the plan of action.
Codes: RET=Retire, REP=Replace, USE=Use Without an Update
EQUIPMENT_INV_6914.Y2K_ASSIGNED_SHOP: The ENGINEERING SECTION that has been assigned responsibility for making this device Y2K compliant. This is the section to which the Y2K work order will be assigned. If this field is not populated then Y2K work orders will be assigned to the RESPONSIBLE SHOP (first entry) if one exists. If their is neither a Y2K ASSIGNED SHOP nor a RESPONSIBLE SHOP, then the Y2K work order will be assigned to the primary biomedical engineering section.
EQUIPMENT_INV_6914.Y2K_CATEGORY: FC =>  Fully compliant. Device will function properly in all respects on January 1, 2000 without user intervention. CC =>  Conditionally compliant. Device requires user intervention to function properly in all respects on January 1, 2000. This may include a manufacturer software and/or hardware update or other one-time user action. NC =>  Non-compliant. Device will not function properly on January 1, 2000 and no known remedy is available. NA =>  Not applicable. There are no Y2K implications for this device.
Codes: FC=FULLY COMPLIANT, CC=CONDITIONALLY COMPLIANT, NC=NON-COMPLIANT, NA=NOT APPLICABLE
EQUIPMENT_INV_6914.Y2K_COMPLIANCE_WORK_O: Whenever a Y2K work order is created (in routine ENY2K5) this field (and its regular cross-reference) in the Equipment File is populated via hard code. THIS FIELD SHOULD NEVER BE DELETED AS LONG AS Y2K IS AN ISSUE.  To avert possible confusion, no Y2K work order number will ever be assigned to more than one piece of equipment. In like manner, no piece of equipment will ever have more than one Y2K work order number. If more than one shop needs to work on the same piece of equipment for Y2K compliance, then the work order will be assigned to the primary shop and other shops will charge their time and materials to this primary work order.  If a Y2K work order is closed inappropriately, it can always be re-opened and corrected via the Edit Work Order option [ENWOEDIT].
Automatically populated with original Y2K work order number.
EQUIPMENT_INV_6914.Y2K_ESTIMATED_REPLACE: Date by which site plans to replace this item with something that is Y2K compliant.
EQUIPMENT_INV_6914.Y2K_FUNCTIONAL_CLASSI: A classification agreed on by the VA and its oversight agencies for Y2K compliance reporting.  PC =>  A general purpose personal computer or workstation used for office applications. Not an integral part of a medical device or of a facility management system.  MED => Medical devices are pieces of equipment (or equipment systems) that are dedicated to the diagnosis and/or treatment of patients. Includes anything that requires Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approval as a medical device before it can be commercially marketed to health care providers in the United States.  FS =>  Facility systems (or facility equipment) are devices (or equipment systems) used to manage the environment of care within health care facilities. Includes building service equipment of all types, such as: o Emergency communications management systems o Security systems o Alarm systems o Fire detection and control systems o Environmental control systems o Water management o Electrical energy management and control systems o Building transport systems (people and/or material)  TEL => Telecommunications equipment, broadly defined. This classification includes PBX systems, voice mail, radio frequency communication systems, faxes, routers, switches, bridges, servers, modems, satellite communication systems, video conferencing, and wireless LAN.
Codes: PC=General purpose workstation, MED=Medical device, FS=Facility equipment, TEL=Telecommunications equipment
EQUIPMENT_INV_6914.Y2K_NOTES: This free text field (80 char max) is intended for use with conditionally compliant and non-compliant devices only. If populated, it will be appended to the COMMENTS field and printed on the Y2K worklist (for conditionally compliant equipment).  Sites are not required to use this field.
EQUIPMENT_INV_6914.Y2K_TECHNICIAN: The engineering employee who is personally responsible for implementation of the Y2K upgrade. This field should be populated only for Y2K CONDITIONALLY COMPLIANT devices and will be used (if it exists) by the system whenever Y2K worklists are printed.
EQUIPMENT_INV_6914.Y2K_UTILITY_SYSTEM: Indicate which devices in a facilities equipment inventory are included in some kind of Facility Management System.  Whenever a user enters a Y2K UTILITY SYSTEM for an entry that is a PARENT of other equipment entries, then AEMS/MERS will automatically assign that Y2K UTILITY SYSTEM to all descendents of that parent entry.  The Y2K UTILITY SYSTEM field will have special significance in centralized reporting of Y2K compliance activities, but the utility of this classification scheme is expected to outlive the Y2K compliance effort.  Some specific examples of utility systems are as follows:  ALARM          o Hazardous Materials o X-Rays and Nuclear Radiation o Biomedical Hazards o Operating Room Gases o Infectious Disease Controls o Biohazard Detection and Control o Gas Detection (carbon monoxide, radon, ozone, etc.)  COMM           o Emergency Dispatching and Communications o Nurse Call Systems  ELECT          o Uninterruptible Power Supplies o Emergency Generators o Power Distribution Units o Lighting Controls o Emergency Lighting  ENVRN          o Heating o Ventilating o Air Conditioning o Load Balancing o Humidification and Dehumidification o Programmable Thermostats  FIRE           o Fire Alarms o Sprinklers o Halon Systems  OTHER          o Laboratory Controls o Remote Data Collection o Traffic Management o Automotive Systems o Machine Controls o Clock Systems o Mail Handling Systems o Microfilming o Records Control o Document Imaging o Copiers  SCRTY          o Passkey Systems o Access Control o Intrusion Detection o Traffic Monitoring o Gates, Doors, Vaults o Employee/Client Identification and Verification o Patient Tracking Systems o Video Monitoring and Time Stamping o Time Card and Check-in Systems o Communications to Security Agencies  TRANS          o Elevators o Escalators o Slideways o Pneumatic Tube Systems o Robotic Devices o Moving Walkways  WATER          o Heating o Cooling o Purification o Pumping o Storage
EQUIPMENT_INV_6914.YALD_CODE: NOTE: This field is not used and it will be deleted by a future version.
FEDERAL_SUPPLY_CLASSIFICATION441_2.ABBRE: This is an abbreviated Federal Supply Classification description.
FEDERAL_SUPPLY_CLASSIFICATION441_2.COMMO: This is the FSC commodity code.
Codes: 1=Drugs, 2=Other Medical, 3=General, 6=Fuel, 8=Subsistence, 9=Unposted Building Supplies, D=Deleted Code
FEDERAL_SUPPLY_CLASSIFICATION441_2.DLA_A: This field restricts the selection to DLA addresses only.
FEDERAL_SUPPLY_CLASSIFICATION441_2.GROUP: This is a pointer to the file of FSC group categories.
FEDERAL_SUPPLY_CLASSIFICATION441_2.NUMBE: This is the 4-character long Federal Supply Classification (FSC) code or Product Service Code (PSC).
MANUFACTURER_LIST_FILE6912.CITY: City to which correspondence could be directed.
MANUFACTURER_LIST_FILE6912.DIVISION: Separate operating unit of the manufacturing company.  For use when appropriate.
MANUFACTURER_LIST_FILE6912.MFGDIV: The original manufacturer of equipment to be accounted for by the facility.  Not to be confused with the vendor.
MANUFACTURER_LIST_FILE6912.MFGID: Internal entry number (IEN) of the manufacturer.  Additions made by sites must be in the range of 50000 to 99999.  National entries start at 1 and presently go up to about 5000.
MANUFACTURER_LIST_FILE6912.STATE: State to which correspondence could be directed.
MANUFACTURER_LIST_FILE6912.STREET: Street address to which correspondence could be directed.
NATIONAL_EIL6914_9.ADMINISTRATIVEOFFICE: Administrative/Office (A/O) for the EIL. If a value is entered here then FA Documents whose CMR value starts with the EIL are required to use this A/O. This field should be left blank if there is more than one appropriate A/O code for the EIL.
NATIONAL_EIL6914_9.CODE: Two digit Equipment Inventory Listing (EIL) code established by VACO Directive.
NATIONAL_EIL6914_9.COST_CENTER: Cost Center (if any) that is linked to the EIL code. This will be used as the cost center of any equipment entries whose CMR begins with the national EIL code.
NX_BOC6914_4.CAPITALIZED_BUDGET_OBJECT_C: In FMS all personal property assets, whether capitalized or expensed, are to be coded to Budget Object Class 31. Only capitalized assets are to be recorded in the Fixed Assets Package.
NX_BOC6914_4.CORRESPONDING_SGL: Standard General Ledger Account corresponding to this Budget Object Code.
NX_BOC6914_4.DEACTIVATED_DATE: As of the date entered in this field, new FA or FR Documents can't be sent to Fixed Assets (Austin) with this BOC.
NX_FUND6914_6.ABBREVIATION: Abbreviation for the fund that could be used to further identify the .01 field when there is not room for the fullfund description.
NX_FUND6914_6.ASSOCIATED_FUND: This field can be used to link an inventory fund in this file with an associated acquisition fund when the first four characters of the associated funds are dissimilar. For example, this field provides a means to associate acquisition funds that start with 0160 (i.e. 0160A1, etc.) with the corresponding inventory fund AMAFMC by entering "0161" in this field for fund AMAFMC. This field is used when the system automatically populates the FUND field in the equipment file based on information from a purchase order/receiving report.
NX_FUND6914_6.DEACTIVATED_DATE: As of the date entered in this field, new FA or FR Documents can't be sent to Fixed Assets (Austin) with this FUND.
NX_FUND6914_6.REVOVLING_FUND: If REVOLVING FUND? is YES, then BEG_BUDGET_FY must be 94 when transmitting documents to FAP.
NX_SGL6914_3.ABBREVIATION: Abbreviation for account that could be used to further identify the .01 field when there is not room for the full account description.
NX_SGL6914_3.DEACTIVATED_DATE: As of the date entered in this field, new FA Documents can't be sent to Austin with this SGL.
NX_SGL6914_3.FA_TYPE: Fixed Asset Type as defined in the Fixed Asset Package of the Financial Management System.
PM_PROCEDURES6914_2.PM_REFERENCE: This reference identifies the PM procedure and is similar in concept to a memo number (e.g. EL-1). It will be shown on PM worklists along with the PM title.
PM_PROCEDURES6914_2.PROCEDURE_TITLE: This is the title of the PM procedure. It will be shown on PM worklists and also in the Work Performed field of PM work orders.
PM_PROCEDURES6914_2.SOURCE: Source of the PM instructions. Could be the equipment manufacturer or some authoritative and/or knowledgeable organization (ex: ASHE, VACO, NEMA, etc). Use of this field is optional.
SERVICESECTION49.ABBREVIATION: This field contains the accepted abbreviation for this service or section.
SERVICESECTION49.AMBULATORY_CARE_FLAG: This field contains the ambulatory care flag.  Yes or No for this sertice or section.
Codes: Y=AMBULATORY CARE, N=NOT AMBULATORY CARE
SERVICESECTION49.ASST_CHIEF: This field contains a pointer to the name of the assistant chief of this service or section.
SERVICESECTION49.CHIEF: This field contains a pointer to the name of the chief of this service or section.
SERVICESECTION49.COORDINATOR_IRM: This field is used by kernel to link a NEW PERSON entry through the service/section pointer back to a New Person entry for access help.
SERVICESECTION49.COST_CENTER: This field contains the cost center name for this service section. The cost center must be defined in the IFCAP Cost Center File 420.1.
SERVICESECTION49.LOCATION: This field contains the physical location of this service or section (i.e., room number).
SERVICESECTION49.MAIL_SYMBOL: This field contains the accepted mail routing symbol for the service or section.
SERVICESECTION49.MIS_COSTING_CODE: This field contains the Management Information Cost Accounting code for this service or section.
SERVICESECTION49.NAME: Field .01: NAME
Enter Service or Section name.
SERVICESECTION49.NATIONAL_SERVICE: This field is a pointer to the National Service File #730, and is Used to link the locally built 'Service/Section' file to the standardized list of nationally recognized services.
SERVICESECTION49.PARENT_SERVICE: This field contains a pointer to the name of the service or section which is "parent" to this section.
SERVICESECTION49.TYPE_OF_COSTING_SECTION: This field contains the type of management information cost accounting section for this service or section.
Codes: A=ADMINISTRATIVE, S=SUB-SPECIALTY ADMINISTRATIVE, O=OFF-STATION, N=NON-ADMINISTRATIVE
SERVICESECTION49.TYPE_OF_SERVICE: This flag indicates the type of each entry in this file. Services or sub-services may be marked as Administrative or for Patient Care.
SOURCE_CODE420_8.ABBREVIATION: This is the abbreviation for the code.
SOURCE_CODE420_8.AGENCY_CODE: This field is used for federal receiving reports.
SOURCE_CODE420_8.CODE: This is the code identifying the procurement source for goods.  The code is used to update centralized reporting for procurement and define either specific government sources (i.e., Depot, GSA), or methods of procuring goods from external sources (i.e., goods procured via government contract).
SOURCE_CODE420_8.DESCRIPTION: This is the description of the source code.
SOURCE_CODE420_8.FISCAL_EQUIV_: This is the fiscal equivalent for this code.
SUB_EQUIPMENT_HISTORY6914_02.HISTORY_REF: Reflects date on which Work Order was posted to EQUIPMENT INV. file, and type of work performed.
SUB_EQUIPMENT_HISTORY6914_02.HOURS_SPENT: Total hours spent in completion of subject work order.  Calculated by a routine that runs automatically when work orders are closed out.
SUB_EQUIPMENT_HISTORY6914_02.LABOR_: Labor cost associated with subject work order.  Calculated on the basis of wage information from the Engineering Employee File by a routine that runs automatically when work orders are closed out.
SUB_EQUIPMENT_HISTORY6914_02.MATERIAL_: Cost of materials used in performing this work action.  Data is manually entered into the Work Order File and automatically extracted from the work order into the Equipment History when the work order is closed out.
SUB_EQUIPMENT_HISTORY6914_02.PM_STATUS: If this posting is the result of a preventive maintenance (PM) inspection, this field should be used to indicate the outcome of that PM.  Field should be left blank in cases of regular (unscheduled) work action.
Codes: P=PASS, C=CORRECTIVE ACTION TAKEN/REQUESTED, D0=DEFERRED, D1=DEFERRED, COULD NOT LOCATE, D2=DEFERRED, IN USE, D3=DEFERRED, OUT OF SERVICE OR LOANED OUT
SUB_EQUIPMENT_HISTORY6914_02.VENDOR_: Amount paid to vendor on account of subject work action.  Entered manually (if applicable) when work orders are closed out.
SUB_EQUIPMENT_HISTORY6914_02.WORKER: First 15 characters of the name of the PRIMARY TECHNICIAN as it appears in the Engineering Employee File.
SUB_EQUIPMENT_HISTORY6914_02.WORK_PERFOR: Brief description of what was done via subject work action.  Automatically extracted from the Work Order File.
SUB_EQUIPMENT_HISTORY6914_02.W_O__REFERE: The number of the Engineering work order that resulted in this posting.
SUB_FA_GROUP6914_31.FA_GROUP: This multiple contains the FA GROUPs that are valid for the SGL (FA TYPE).
SUB_FREQUENCY6914_43.FREQUENCY: Make a separate entry for each category (MONTHLY, QUARTERLY, etc.) of PMI that is to be scheduled for this device. The PM module looks at this field in conjunction with the STARTING MONTH when PM lists are generated. Let's consider a fairly complex example: a device with SEMI-ANNUAL, QUARTERLY, and MONTHLY PMI's and a STARTING MONTH of MAR. Assuming no entry for SKIP MONTHS, the following PMI's will be scheduled: SEMI-ANNUAL in MAR and SEP; QUARTERLY in JUN and DEC; MONTHLY in APR, MAY, JUL, AUG, OCT, NOV, JAN and FEB.
Codes: A=ANNUAL, S=SEMI-ANNUAL, Q=QUARTERLY, M=MONTHLY, BM=BI-MONTHLY, W=WEEKLY, BW=BI-WEEKLY, N=NONE, BA=BI-ANNUAL, TA=TRI-ANNUAL
SUB_FREQUENCY6914_43.HOURS_Estimated: Approximate amount of time required for this PMI(standard hours), to the nearest tenth of an hour. This value will be recorded in the EQUIPMENT HISTORY field when a PM is closed out unless the user chooses to explicitly enter another (more precise) value.
SUB_FREQUENCY6914_43.LEVEL3: Each scheduled PMI may be composed of some combination of one or more of the following discrete levels of activity: Level 1 - Visual inspection only; Level 2 - Check and adjust operator controls; Level 3 - Electrical safety analysis; Level 4 - Minor parts replacement; Level 5 - Major parts replacement; Level 6 - Complete overhaul. LEVEL is an optional field and is intended to accommodate the needs of certain facilities with highly developed PM programs. Entries for LEVEL (if any) will be printed on the PM worklist as a reminder to the responsible technician. If more than one number applies, separate numbers a comma.
SUB_FREQUENCY6914_43.MATERIAL_COST_Estim: Estimated material cost for this PMI (standard cost). This cost will be charged to the piece of equipment whenever a PM of this type is closed out unless another (more precise) value is entered at close-out time.
SUB_FREQUENCY6914_43.PROCEDURE4: Enter the abbreviation (4 to 10 characters) of the PROCEDURE to be followed in performing this category of PMI on this device. The title (as well as the abreviation) of the PM PROCEDURE will appear on PM worksheets for reference. If disk space permits, the actual procedure itself may be entered in the TEXT field of the PM PROCEDURES file (Number 6914.2) and printed on demand. In any event, the procedure should be on file and readily accessible to the technician performing the work.
SUB_FREQUENCY6914_43.STARTING_YEAR_4_num: This field has meaning only for BI-ANNUAL and TRI-ANNUAL frequencies. STARTING YEAR must be entered as four numeric characters (ex: 1998, 2002, etc.).
SUB_IT_COMMENTS6914_092.IT_COMMENTS: This field contains comments entered by IT staff concerning an IT equipment record.
SUB_ORIGINAL_BAR_CODE_ID6914_05.ORIGINAL: The original bar code identifier. This field is normally populated only in cases where a site undergoes consolidation with another facility. In such a case, the routines used to merge the site's equipment records with those of the primary site will record an image of the original bar code label so that the Engineering Package will still be able to recognize it. This will enable sites affected by merger to continue to use their bar coded inventory and preventive maintenance functions without replacing existing bar coded equipment labels.  The format of this field is of the form 'SSS EENNNN', where SSS is the station number and NNNN is the Equipment ID# (also the internal entry number) prior to consolidation. ' EE' is a literal character string used in bar coding all equipment labels.
SUB_RESPONSIBLE_SHOP6914_04.CRITICALITY: An index of the importance of performing PMI's on this device. Enter an integer between 1 and some upper limit not greater than 99 (most sites use 10 or 20). The closer the values are to the upper limit the more critical the PMI's become. A value of 1 would indicate that PMI's are desireable but far from essential (least critical).  When PM worklists are generated, the system will ask if all devices should be included or just those whose CRITICALITY is within a certain user selectable range (say, 7 to 10). This is intended as a means of adjusting workload to match available resources.  Use of this feature is left entirely to the discretion of each site. If a CRITICALITY range is selected, the system will ask the user whether devices having no CRITICALITY should be included or excluded.
SUB_RESPONSIBLE_SHOP6914_04.SKIP_MONTHS: A range of months (inclusive) during which PMI's are to be suspended. For example, an entry of 'NOV-MAR' for an air-conditioner would suppress the scheduling of any PMI's in NOV, DEC, JAN, FEB, and MAR. Some care needs to be taken when using this field. If you want an ANNUAL inspecton, for instance, be sure that the STARTING MONTH is not within the range specified by the SKIP MONTHS; otherwise the ANNUAL PMI will never be scheduled. Entries must take the form 'MMM-NNN', where MMM is a three character abbreviation of the first month for which PMiI's are to be suspended and NNN is a three character abbreviation for the last month for which PMI's are to be suspended. Valid abbreviations are: JAN, FEB, MAR, APR, MAY, JUN, JUL, AUG, SEP, OCT, NOV, and DEC.
SUB_RESPONSIBLE_SHOP6914_04.STARTING_MON: STARTING MONTH is used by the PM module as a criterion for determining when a PM is due. Let's consider a fairly complex example: an item subject to MONTHLY, QUARTERLY, and ANNUAL PM inspections. If STARTING MONTH were set to FEB; an ANNUAL inspection would be scheduled in FEB; QUARTERLY inspections in MAY, AUG, and NOV; and MONTHLY inspections in MAR, APR, JUN, JUL, SEP, OCT, DEC, and JAN. If STARTING MONTH is left blank, JAN will be assumed.
SUB_RESPONSIBLE_SHOP6914_04.TECHNICIAN: The Engineering Service employee who normally does the PM work on this piece of equipment for this shop.
SUB_SPEX6914_03.SPEX: This field is normally used to store comments by A&MM (PPM) peronnel. It is shown on the Equipment Inventory Listing (EIL) report.
UTILITY_SYSTEMS6918_1.FULL_NAME: The fully expanded name of the utility system.
UTILITY_SYSTEMS6918_1.NAME: Field .01: NAME
Abbreviated (5 character max, uppercase only) designation of utility systems commonly recognized in Facility Management operations. Fields length is kept short to facilitate screen entry.
WORK_ORDER_6920.BED_: Optional field. Filled in at time of request if the work requested is associated with a specific bed in a patient room.
WORK_ORDER_6920.CONTACT_PERSON: This is the person to be contacted if there are questions about the nature of the work that has been requested.
WORK_ORDER_6920.DATE_ASSIGNED: Date on which work order was assigned to the current shop.
WORK_ORDER_6920.DATE_COMPLETE_or_closed: Date on which work order is closed out.
WORK_ORDER_6920.ENTERED_BY: Identifies the user who actually entered the work request. Field is automatically populated when work order is entered via Electronic Work Order Module.
WORK_ORDER_6920.EQUIPMENT_ID: Entry in the Equipment File (#6914) to which this work order is to be charged.
WORK_ORDER_6920.EQUIPMENT_MANUFACTURER: This field is no longer used and it will be deleted by a future release. (Text representation of manufacturer. Used to be automatically triggered.)
WORK_ORDER_6920.LOCAL_IDENTIFIER: This optional field may contain any type of identifier that has meaning at your site.
WORK_ORDER_6920.LOCATION: Physical location where work is to be performed.
WORK_ORDER_6920.MODEL: Model number assigned to equipment under repair by the manufacturer.
WORK_ORDER_6920.NOTIFICATION_MESSAGE: This field contains the message number of a computer generated notification message sent to the requester. Any further notification messages are sent as responses to this message.
WORK_ORDER_6920.NOTIFICATION_PREFERENCE: This field will be checked to determine if a mail message should be sent to the requestor when the status of an electronic work order is modified. ENG SOFTWARE OPTIONS 'NOTIFY W.O. REQUESTOR' must be 'A' for this field to be asked during entry of a electronic work order. Note that a mail message will always be sent when a work order is disapproved.
Codes: C=COMPLETED STATUS, S=STATUS CHANGED, N=NO MESSAGE
WORK_ORDER_6920.ORIGINAL_WORK_ORDER_: This field is automatically populated whenever a new work request is entered. Unlike the .01 field, the 'ORIGINAL WORK ORDER #' will not be affected if the work request is transferred from one shop to another. The main purpose of this field is to allow requesters outside of Engineering Service to check on the status of work requests which they enter themselves. If requesters make a note of the WORK ORDER #'s assigned to their work requests as they enter them, they will always be able to use these original numbers to check the status.
WORK_ORDER_6920.OWNERDEPARTMENT: The service or section for whom work is to be performed.
WORK_ORDER_6920.PARTS_ORDERED_ON_ACC_: The Control Point Activity Transaction for parts or services required to complete this task.
WORK_ORDER_6920.PHONE: Telephone number or extension of the individual requesting the work.
WORK_ORDER_6920.PMI_NUMBER: Property Management Number.  Applicable only to work requests that are chargeable to equipment.  This data element is likely to be phased out in the near future.
WORK_ORDER_6920.PM_STATUS: Outcome of preventive maintenance inspection.  Useable for PM work orders only.
Codes: P=PASS, C=CORRECTIVE ACTION TAKEN/REQUESTED, D0=DEFERRED, D1=DEFERRED, COULD NOT LOCATE, D2=DEFERRED, IN USE, D3=DEFERRED, OUT OF SERVICE OR LOANED OUT
WORK_ORDER_6920.PRIMARY_TECH_ASSIGNED: Technician who bears primary responsibility for completion of task.
WORK_ORDER_6920.PRIORITY: Relative priority of this work request.
Codes: E=EMERGENCY, H=HIGH, A=AVERAGE, L=LOW, M=MODIFICATION
WORK_ORDER_6920.REQUEST_DATE: Date (and time if desired) when work request was originally entered.
WORK_ORDER_6920.REQUEST_MODE: Indicator of how the work was actually requested.
Codes: P=PHONE, W=WRITTEN, D=DELIVERED, V=VERBAL, C=COMPUTER
WORK_ORDER_6920.SERIAL_NO_: Serial number of affected equipment.  Assigned by manufacturer.
WORK_ORDER_6920.SHOP: The Engineering Section to which the Work Order is assigned.
WORK_ORDER_6920.STATUS: Added with Version 6.4. May be helpful when printing reports of M&R activity.
Codes: 1=IN PROGRESS, 2=PENDING, 3=WAITING ON PARTS, 4=WAITING ON VENDOR SERVICE, 5=DISAPPROVED, 6=COMPLETED
WORK_ORDER_6920.TASK_DESCRIPTION_60_char: A brief statement that describes the work being requested.
WORK_ORDER_6920.TOTAL_HOURS: Total man-hours by all assigned employees.  Calculated by the system automatically.
WORK_ORDER_6920.TOTAL_LABOR_COST: Total labor cost chargeable to this work order.  System will compute this value by multiplying the HOURS of each TECHNICIAN ASSIGNED times his WAGE and totaling the results.
WORK_ORDER_6920.TOTAL_MATERIAL_COST: Approximate cost of materials needed to complete this task.
WORK_ORDER_6920.VENDOR_SERVICE_COST: Approximate cost of vendor services needed to complete this task.
WORK_ORDER_6920.WORK_CENTER_CODE: Category of task to which this work order most closely corresponds.
WORK_ORDER_6920.WORK_ORDER_: Identifier of each individual work action.  Composed of the shop abbreviation, date generated, and a computer generated sequential component.  Users may delete work orders when necessary, but they should never change a work order number.
WORK_ORDER_6920.WORK_PERFORMED_140_char_: Brief description of work actually performed (may be extracted from COMMENTS field). The WORK PERFORMED field will be saved in the EQUIPMENT (Inventory) File (No. 6914) where it will be a permanent part of the device history. In contrast, the COMMENTS field will be removed from disk (on-line) storage when the work order is archived.
